forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). v1.0 / CORRECTED do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions 'low' gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one. For growth assumptions (projection, system_needs, capacity price growth) low/high = lower/higher growth. Scenarios (Cautious / Central / Ambitious) set the programs, deferral and load_enabled layers together and hold growth assumptions and the utility share at central.

Cautious.description: Today's programs grown modestly, no flexible connections, high cost per kW-year, low locational match; growth and utility share central.

Central.description: Every assumption at central; flexible MW anchored to state potential study (Brattle for NYSERDA/DPS).

Ambitious.description: DOE national range (20% of peak) or the state anchor if higher, low cost per kW-year, high locational match, more flexible connections; growth and utility share central.

supply_energy_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE (flat real energy prices)

transmission_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE; high reflects transmission build-out

program_surcharge_growth.source: Assumption: BAU surcharge rates grow with inflation (policy-driven)

ev_share_of_electrification.source: NREL Electrification Futures Study: transportation is 1,424 of 1,782 TWh (80%) of the 2050 increase in the High scenario and 810 of 932 TWh (87%) in Medium
ev_share_of_electrification.note: Reconciliation: the notebook ramp is TOTAL electrification (its sources cite EVs and heat pumps). It is split 80% EVs / 20% buildings and other using the EFS High-scenario sector split, so both segments contribute and total electrification equals the v1.0 load forecast. The EV count curve is no longer used for energy (at 3,600 kWh/EV it implied more energy than the whole ramp for Con Edison, RG&E and Pepco).

network_bands.unit: bands of substation loading, most to least loaded: share of firm capacity, starting loading (network peak / firm capacity); growth_share and flex_share optional (default pro rata to load)
network_bands.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3: substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general; capacity net of a 0.70 x largest-transformer N-1 reserve); 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation (load / (0.80 x rating - contract reserves)), the filing's definition of a constrained feeder. No published utility-wide loading distribution found: NYSEG/RG&E publish feeder hosting-capacity maps but no aggregate distribution; Dominion's measured distribution (the only US utility-wide figure found) is used as a proxy. Replace with utility data.

ramp_pct_peak_dr.unit: maximum MW added per year, share of the utility's 2026 peak (null = no cap)
ramp_pct_peak_dr.source: Observed ramp: Pepco Energy Wise Rewards direct load control added 50 MW in 2010 (EmPOWER Maryland 2011 report, Table 16) and 44 MW in 2011 (2012 report, Table 16), its fastest build-out = 50 / 3,644 MW Pepco MD peak = 1.37% of peak per year (central). Long-run 2009-2025: 0 to 247 MW (2026 EmPOWER report, Table 13) = 14.5 MW/yr = 0.40% of peak per year (low, Cautious). High (Ambitious): no cap, the target path applies. Expressed as a share of each utility's 2026 peak

capacity_carve_out.source: NYISO Rest of State (RG&E is in Load Zone B) monthly spot capacity prices, 2026: May $8.00, Jul $4.14, Sep $5.97/kW-month (Modo Energy NYISO monthly reports); mean $6.0367/kW-month x 12 = $0.07244M/MW-yr. v1.0 uses NYISO.json zone G_H_I ($0.070M/MW-yr) for RG&E; that default is unchanged. Peak: RGE.json. Residential share and customers: EIA-861 2024. Scaling 1.0 (NYISO reserve margin not applied).
capacity_carve_out.method: Residential capacity obligation per customer = peak_mw x residential_share x obligation_scaling / residential_customers; $/month = obligation (kW) x price ($/kW-day) x 365/12. Assumes the residential share of the obligation equals its share of sales (residential load is peakier, so this likely understates it). The amount is moved out of the parent line(s); the total bill is unchanged.
